title: 06. Memory, State & HITL: Day 5 — Streaming and Message History
summary: A 500-token email drafted in 8 seconds feels slow. The same email printed token-by-token over 8 seconds feels responsive — users see progress and can stop the model the moment it goes off the rails.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: A 500-token email drafted in 8 seconds feels slow. The same email printed token-by-token over 8 seconds feels responsive — users see progress and can stop the model the moment it goes off the rails. Pydantic AI gives you three streaming primitives: `agent.run_stream()` for the final result, `agent.iter()` for the full event stream (model requests, tool calls, returns, final result), and low-level helpers like `stream_text()` for fine control. Today you will use all three, then layer on **`message_history`** to build true multi-turn conversations.

sections.title: Why Streaming?
sections.body:
Three reasons:

1. **Perceived latency.** First-token-in-300ms beats full-response-in-3-seconds, even if total time is identical.
2. **Long generations.** A 2,000-token summary might take 15 seconds. Users assume the app is frozen.
3. **Early termination.** Cancel and restart if the model hallucinates mid-response.

The tradeoff: streaming requires `async`. Pydantic AI makes it as painless as possible.

sections.title: agent.run_stream() — Streaming the Final Result
sections.body:
For most use cases, `run_stream()` is what you want. It returns an async context manager that yields chunks of the final result.

```python
import asyncio
from pydantic_ai import Agent

poet = Agent("openai:gpt-4o-mini", system_prompt="You write short poems.")

async def main() -> None:
    async with poet.run_stream("A haiku about dependency injection") as result:
        async for chunk in result.stream():
            print(chunk, end="", flush=True)
    print()  # newline after final chunk

asyncio.run(main())
```

`result.stream()` yields `str` chunks as they arrive. `result.stream_text()` is an alias when the result type is text. Call `result.get()` after the loop to retrieve the full final string if you need it later.

For structured (non-text) result types, `run_stream()` yields partial objects via `result.stream_responses()` — Pydantic AI reconstructs the partial model from incoming tokens. Useful for "live updating" a UI with a half-built JSON object.

sections.title: agent.iter() — The Full Event Stream
sections.body:
`iter()` exposes everything: every model request, every tool call, every tool return, and the final result. Use it when you need to visualize, log, or react to intermediate steps.

```python
import asyncio
from datetime import datetime
from pydantic_ai import Agent, RunContext

researcher = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    system_prompt="Use the tools to answer. Be brief.",
)

@researcher.tool
def get_weather(ctx: RunContext[None], city: str) -> str:
    """Return the weather for a city."""
    return f"Sunny, 22C in {city}"

@researcher.tool
def get_time(ctx: RunContext[None], tz: str) -> str:
    """Return current time in a timezone."""
    return f"It is afternoon in {tz}"

async def main() -> None:
    started = datetime.now()
    async with researcher.iter("What's the weather in Paris and time in UTC?") as run:
        async for event in run:
            ts = (datetime.now() - started).total_seconds()
            kind = event.kind  # e.g. "tool_call", "tool_return", "final_result"
            print(f"[{ts:5.2f}s] {kind}: {event!r}")
    print("Final:", run.result.data if run.result else "<no result>")

asyncio.run(main())
```

Each event has a `.kind` string. The ones you will see most often:

- **`tool_call`** — model wants to call a tool. Inspect `event.tool_name` and `event.args`.
- **`tool_return`** — tool finished. Inspect `event.result`.
- **`model_request`** — agent is about to call the model.
- **`model_response`** — model replied (with tool calls or text).
- **`final_result`** — agent produced the final answer.

The exact event class names depend on Pydantic AI version, but `event.kind` is stable. Use it for switching.

sections.title: Example 1: Live Email Drafter with rich.live
sections.body:
Combine `run_stream()` with `rich.live` for a typewriter effect. Install with `pip install rich`.

```python
# live_email.py
import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal

from rich.console import Console
from rich.live import Live
from rich.panel import Panel
from pydantic_ai import Agent, RunContext

@dataclass
class EmailDeps:
    user_name: str
    user_tone: Literal["formal", "casual"]
    signature: str

drafter = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    deps_type=EmailDeps,
    system_prompt="Draft a short email. Match the user's tone. Sign with the signature from context.",
)

@drafter.tool
def finalize_email(ctx: RunContext[EmailDeps], body: str) -> str:
    """Wrap the drafted body with the user's signature."""
    return f"{body}\n\n— {ctx.deps.user_name}\n{ctx.deps.signature}"

async def main() -> None:
    deps = EmailDeps(user_name="Ada", user_tone="formal",
                     signature="Founder, Analytical Engines Inc.")
    console = Console()
    buffer: list[str] = []

    with Live(Panel("Thinking…"), console=console, refresh_per_second=20) as live:
        async with drafter.run_stream("Draft a thank-you note to Charles.", deps=deps) as result:
            async for chunk in result.stream_text():
                buffer.append(chunk)
                live.update(Panel("".join(buffer), title="Drafting email"))

    final = await result.get()
    console.print(Panel(final, title="Final email", border_style="green"))

asyncio.run(main())
```

The `Live` widget re-renders the panel on each chunk — users see the email assemble itself.

sections.title: Example 2: Tool Call Visualizer with iter()
sections.body:
This script prints a structured trace of every event with timing — invaluable for debugging why an agent made weird tool choices.

```python
# trace_agent.py
import asyncio
from datetime import datetime

from pydantic_ai import Agent, RunContext

weather_agent = Agent("openai:gpt-4o-mini", system_prompt="Use tools to answer.")

@weather_agent.tool
def temperature(ctx: RunContext[None], city: str) -> int:
    """Return temperature in Celsius for a city."""
    return 22 if city.lower().startswith("par") else 18

@weather_agent.tool
def humidity(ctx: RunContext[None], city: str) -> int:
    """Return humidity percentage for a city."""
    return 55

async def main() -> None:
    start = datetime.now()
    print(f"{'ELAPSED':>8} | {'EVENT':<15} | DETAIL")
    print("-" * 60)
    async with weather_agent.iter("What is the temperature and humidity in Paris?") as run:
        async for event in run:
            elapsed = (datetime.now() - start).total_seconds()
            kind = event.kind
            detail = ""
            if kind == "tool_call":
                detail = f"{event.tool_name}({event.args})"
            elif kind == "tool_return":
                detail = f"-> {event.result!r}"
            elif kind == "final_result":
                detail = "(final)"
            print(f"{elapsed:8.2f} | {kind:<15} | {detail}")
    print("-" * 60)
    print("Final answer:", run.result.data)

asyncio.run(main())
```

Sample output:

```
ELAPSED  | EVENT           | DETAIL
------------------------------------------------------------
   0.12  | model_request   |
   0.85  | tool_call       | temperature({'city': 'Paris'})
   0.86  | tool_return     | -> 22
   0.87  | model_request   |
   1.42  | tool_call       | humidity({'city': 'Paris'})
   1.43  | tool_return     | -> 55
   1.44  | model_request   |
   2.10  | final_result    | (final)
```

You can see the model issued tool calls serially. With prompt tweaks ("call all needed tools at once") you can sometimes get them in parallel.

sections.title: Message History: Multi-Turn Conversations
sections.body:
A real chatbot keeps context across turns. Re-sending the entire conversation as a single prompt each turn wastes tokens and confuses the model. Pydantic AI tracks messages for you.

The pattern:

1. Turn 1: `result1 = await agent.run("Hi, I'm Ada")` — agent sees only the user prompt.
2. Turn 2: `result2 = await agent.run("What's my name?", message_history=result1.all_messages())` — agent sees turn 1's full exchange plus the new prompt.

Two helpers on every `RunResult`:

- **`result.all_messages()`** — every message (system, user, model, tool) from this run, in order.
- **`result.new_messages()`** — only the messages produced during this run (not the ones passed in via `message_history`).
- **`result.new_messages_json()`** / **`result.all_messages_json()`** — JSON-serialized bytes, for persisting to Redis/Postgres.

```python
import asyncio
from pydantic_ai import Agent

chat = Agent("openai:gpt-4o-mini", system_prompt="You are a friendly assistant.")

async def main() -> None:
    r1 = await chat.run("Hi, my name is Ada and I love analytical engines.")
    print("Turn 1:", r1.data)

    r2 = await chat.run("What's my name and what do I love?",
                        message_history=r1.all_messages())
    print("Turn 2:", r2.data)

    r3 = await chat.run("Summarize what I told you so far.",
                        message_history=r2.all_messages())
    print("Turn 3:", r3.data)

asyncio.run(main())
```

Each turn, `all_messages()` grows by the new user message plus the model's reply. Pass the full history on every subsequent turn.

sections.title: Example 3: Two-Turn Email Assistant
sections.body:
Turn 1 classifies an incoming email; turn 2 drafts a reply using the classification as context.

```python
# two_turn_email.py
import asyncio
from pydantic_ai import Agent

classifier = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    system_prompt="Classify the email as one of: urgent, routine, spam. Reply with just the label.",
)

replier = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    system_prompt="Draft a short reply to the email based on its classification.",
)

async def main() -> None:
    incoming = (
        "Subject: URGENT: production outage\n"
        "The deploy at 3am broke auth. Please help immediately."
    )

    # Turn 1: classify
    r1 = await classifier.run(f"Classify this email:\n\n{incoming}")
    label = r1.data.strip().lower()
    print(f"Classification: {label}")

    # Turn 2: reply, carrying classification context as history
    # We use a fresh replier agent but inject r1's messages as the prefix.
    r2 = await replier.run(
        f"Based on the classification '{label}', draft a 2-sentence reply to this email:\n\n{incoming}",
        message_history=r1.all_messages(),
    )
    print("Reply draft:\n", r2.data)

asyncio.run(main())
```

This is the simplest multi-agent handoff: two agents share history. By Day 7 you will see cleaner delegation patterns.

sections.title: Persisting History Across Processes
sections.body: For a server, you cannot hold `RunResult` in memory across requests. Serialize with `result.new_messages_json()` (bytes) and store in Redis/Postgres. On the next request, deserialize using `ModelMessage.model_validate_json(...)` from `pydantic_ai.messages` and pass the list as `message_history=`. Use `new_messages()` (only this turn's additions) for append-only logs; use `all_messages()` to reload from zero.

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
- **Streaming requires `async`.** You cannot use `run_stream()` from sync code. If you are inside FastAPI, declare your route `async def`. If you must call from sync, use `asyncio.run()` at the boundary.
- **`iter()` events are typed — wrong type hints break runtime.** If you write `event: FinalResultEvent` and the event is actually a `ToolCallEvent`, `isinstance` checks will silently fail. Use `event.kind` string comparison instead.
- **Forgetting `message_history=` on turn 2.** The agent has amnesia and asks "what's your name again?" Always thread `r.all_messages()` from the previous turn.
- **JSON serialization.** `all_messages()` returns Pydantic model instances. Use `all_messages_json()` for safe serialization; do not `json.dumps()` the list directly (it will fail on tool call parts).
- **Mixing agents in a shared history.** If agent A produced the history and you pass it to agent B with a different `result_type`, Pydantic AI may reject or misinterpret messages. Keep history scoped to one agent.
- **`run_stream()` does not call tools before streaming.** If your agent must call tools first, use `iter()` instead and watch for the `final_result` event.
